faqs.q: How much does a Dogo Argentino cost to buy?
faqs.a: Reputable breeders typically charge $1,200–$4,000 for a Dogo Argentino puppy. Prices vary by breeder reputation, health testing, and lineage. Rescue adoption fees are typically $100–$500 and include vaccinations, neutering, and microchipping.

faqs.q: What is the monthly cost of owning a Dogo Argentino?
faqs.a: Budget $200–$400 per month for a Dogo Argentino, covering food, preventive vet care, insurance, grooming and supplies. Large breeds cost more across every category — food portions, medication doses and professional services all scale with weight.

faqs.q: What are the biggest ongoing costs for a Dogo Argentino?
faqs.a: The three largest annual expenses are food ($800–1,200), veterinary care ($400–$1,200 budgeted annually), and pet insurance ($800–1,800 per year). Grooming costs are lower for short-coated breeds managed at home.

faqs.q: How much does a Dogo Argentino cost in the first year?
faqs.a: Year one costs for a Dogo Argentino are significantly higher than subsequent years, typically $2,500–$5,000. This covers the purchase price or adoption fee, initial vet checks, vaccinations, spay/neuter, microchipping, crate, bedding, collar, leads and puppy training classes.

faqs.q: How often should I groom a Dogo Argentino?
faqs.a: Dogo Argentinos need brushing once or twice per week.  Nails should be trimmed every 3–4 weeks. Ears should be checked and cleaned monthly.

faqs.q: Do Dogo Argentinos shed a lot?
faqs.a: Dogo Argentinos shed minimally. A weekly brush is usually sufficient.

faqs.q: What grooming tools does a Dogo Argentino need?
faqs.a: A rubber grooming glove or soft-bristle brush is sufficient for weekly maintenance on the Dogo Argentino's short coat. Add a nail grinder and ear cleaner for a complete grooming kit.

faqs.q: How often should I bathe a Dogo Argentino?
faqs.a: Every 4–6 weeks is appropriate for most Dogo Argentinos that live indoors. More frequent bathing is needed if they swim or spend time in mud. Over-bathing strips natural skin oils — use a pH-balanced dog shampoo rather than human products.

faqs.q: Are Dogo Argentinos easy to train?
faqs.a: Dogo Argentinos are considered easier to train than average — they respond quickly to reward-based methods and generalise cues well. Short 10–15 minute sessions outperform long correction-heavy drills.

faqs.q: What training method works best for a Dogo Argentino?
faqs.a: Reward-based training using treats, praise and toy rewards is the most effective and well-researched approach for Dogo Argentinos. Keep sessions short and positive, end on a success, and vary your rewards to maintain engagement.

faqs.q: At what age should I start training my Dogo Argentino?
faqs.a: Start training from the day your puppy arrives home, typically at 8 weeks. The 8–16 week window is the most sensitive socialisation period. Enrol in a puppy class within the first two weeks for structured socialisation alongside basic obedience foundations.

faqs.q: How long does it take to train a Dogo Argentino?
faqs.a: Most Dogo Argentinos learn basic obedience cues (sit, stay, come, down) within 2–4 weeks of daily practice. Reliable recall in distracting environments typically takes 2–3 months of consistent reinforcement.

faqs.q: What health problems do Dogo Argentinos commonly have?
faqs.a: Dogo Argentinos are most commonly associated with bloat (GDV). Regular vet checks, appropriate weight management, and breed-specific screening tests help detect issues early. Ask any breeder for health test results before purchasing.

faqs.q: How long do Dogo Argentinos live?
faqs.a: Dogo Argentinos have an average lifespan of 9–15 years. Larger breeds typically have shorter lifespans than smaller breeds. Maintaining a healthy weight and regular vet care are the most impactful factors for longevity.

faqs.q: Are Dogo Argentinos prone to hip dysplasia?
faqs.a: Dogo Argentinos have a moderate-to-elevated risk of hip dysplasia, particularly for large or active breeds. Ask for OFA or PennHIP hip evaluation certificates when buying from a breeder. Weight control and avoiding high-impact exercise during bone growth (under 18 months) reduces risk.

faqs.q: What health tests should a Dogo Argentino puppy have?
faqs.a: At minimum, your Dogo Argentino puppy should have a vet health check, first vaccinations, deworming, and microchipping before coming home. Ask the breeder for parent health certificates relevant to Dogo Argentino-specific conditions. A vet check within 72 hours of bringing your puppy home is recommended to establish a baseline.

faqs.q: Are Dogo Argentinos good with kids?
faqs.a: Dogo Argentinos are generally known for being friendly and patient, making them well-suited to family life with children. Supervision is always recommended with young children regardless of breed — interactions should be taught from both sides.

faqs.q: Do Dogo Argentinos get along with other dogs?
faqs.a: Dogo Argentinos are generally sociable with other dogs, particularly when well-socialised from puppyhood. Introduce new dogs on neutral territory and keep initial meetings brief and positive.

faqs.q: Do Dogo Argentinos bark a lot?
faqs.a: Dogo Argentinos tend to be vocal — they may bark at strangers, sounds, or when under-stimulated. Adequate daily exercise and mental enrichment (training sessions, puzzle feeders) significantly reduce nuisance barking. Teaching a "quiet" cue early is worthwhile.

faqs.q: Are Dogo Argentinos good apartment dogs?
faqs.a: Dogo Argentinos are not ideally suited to apartments — their size and energy level need outdoor space and significant daily exercise. If you do have an apartment, plan for 60–90 minutes of outdoor exercise daily and consider doggy daycare for additional stimulation.

faqs.q: How much exercise does a Dogo Argentino need per day?
faqs.a: Dogo Argentinos need approximately 60–90 minutes of exercise daily. Split across at least two sessions daily, with one higher-intensity session (running, fetch, swimming) and one loose-lead sniff walk. Mental exercise (training sessions, puzzle feeders) counts toward overall stimulation needs and can reduce restless behaviour.

faqs.q: Are Dogo Argentinos good running partners?
faqs.a: Yes — Dogo Argentinos make excellent running partners once fully grown (typically 12–18 months for medium breeds, 18–24 months for large breeds). Start with shorter distances and build gradually to protect developing joints.

faqs.q: What happens if a Dogo Argentino doesn't get enough exercise?
faqs.a: Under-exercised Dogo Argentinos often develop destructive behaviours — chewing, digging, excessive barking, and hyperactivity indoors. These are symptoms of frustration, not bad temperament. Two missed exercise sessions back-to-back typically shows up as restlessness or nuisance behaviour.

faqs.q: Can a Dogo Argentino be off-lead?
faqs.a: Off-lead freedom for a Dogo Argentino depends on recall reliability, not breed alone. Train recall from puppyhood using long-line sessions before progressing to full off-lead. A standard 20-foot long-line gives freedom while maintaining safety during the training phase.

faqs.q: How much should I feed my Dogo Argentino?
faqs.a: A Dogo Argentino needs approximately 3–5 cups of dry food per day for an adult, split across two meals. Always follow the feeding guide on your specific formula — calorie density varies significantly between brands. Adjust portions based on body condition: you should be able to feel (but not easily see) the ribs.

faqs.q: How many times a day should I feed a Dogo Argentino?
faqs.a: Adult Dogo Argentinos should eat twice daily. Puppies (under 6 months) need 3–4 smaller meals per day to support growth and prevent hypoglycaemia, particularly in small breeds. For large and giant breeds, twice daily feeding also reduces the risk of bloat (GDV) compared to one large daily meal.

faqs.q: What is the best food for a Dogo Argentino?
faqs.a: Look for a formula carrying an AAFCO adequacy statement for the correct life stage. A named protein source (chicken, turkey, beef, salmon) should appear first in the ingredient list. Active Dogo Argentinos benefit from higher-protein formulas (26–30% crude protein) to support muscle maintenance.

faqs.q: When should I switch my Dogo Argentino from puppy to adult food?
faqs.a: Large breeds should stay on a large-breed puppy formula until 18–24 months, then transition to an adult formula. Switching too early can disrupt joint development during the growth phase.

faqs.q: Is a Dogo Argentino a good dog for first-time owners?
faqs.a: Dogo Argentinos can be challenging for first-time owners due to their size and exercise demands. Prior dog experience or professional training classes from the start significantly improves outcomes. Research the breed thoroughly before committing.

faqs.q: Are Dogo Argentinos good family dogs?
faqs.a: Dogo Argentinos are typically affectionate family dogs that do well with children and adapt to household routines. Their sociable nature means they prefer company over isolation.

faqs.q: Do Dogo Argentinos do well when left alone?
faqs.a: Dogo Argentinos form strong bonds with their owners and do not do well with extended isolation. Aim for no more than 4–6 hours alone at a time. If your schedule requires longer absences, consider a dog walker, doggy daycare, or a companion dog.

faqs.q: How much time do you need for a Dogo Argentino?
faqs.a: Plan for 2–3 hours per day dedicated to your Dogo Argentino — covering exercise, training, feeding and general interaction.  The commitment is consistent year-round, not just when convenient.
